<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-author">Author</button></h2><div id="work-acc-author" class="accordion-collapse collapse show"><div class="accordion-body"><p class="mb-0 work-author"><a href="../poets/rudrabhatta.html">Rudrabhaṭṭa</a></p></div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Śṛṅgāratilaka is a Sanskrit work by Rudrabhaṭṭa, divided into three sections that deal with different aspects of love: Sambhogaśṛṅgāra, Vipralambhaśṛṅgāra, and Hāsyādirasanirūpanā. It provides a comprehensive exploration of the complexities of romantic relationships, covering the pleasures of physical union, the pain of separation, and the humorous situations that can arise between lovers. The work is known for its rich descriptions of human emotions and its use of intricate literary devices to capture the nuances of erotic experience.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Śṛṅgāratilaka is divided into three sections:<br><br>Sambhogaśṛṅgāra: This section deals with the pleasures of physical union between lovers. It describes the various stages of intimacy between a man and a woman, and the different moods and emotions that accompany each stage.<br><br>Vipralambhaśṛṅgāra: This section deals with the pain of separation that lovers experience. It describes the longing, sadness, and despair that come when lovers are separated from each other, either by distance or by circumstances.<br><br>Hāsyādirasanirūpanā: This section deals with the comic aspects of love. It describes the humorous situations that can arise between lovers, and the ways in which they can find joy and laughter in their relationship.<br><br>Each section of the Śṛṅgāratilaka is written in a different poetic style, with the first section in the Prakrit language, the second section in Sanskrit, and the third section in a mix of both languages. The work is known for its rich descriptions of human emotions, and its detailed exploration of the complexities of love and relationships.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Śṛṅgāratilaka is a unique work in the field of Sanskrit literature for its comprehensive exploration of the various aspects of romantic love, which it accomplishes through a combination of intricate literary devices and rich descriptions of human emotions. The work stands out for its detailed depictions of the pleasures and pains of physical union and separation, as well as its humorous treatment of the lighter aspects of love. Additionally, its use of a mix of Sanskrit and Prakrit languages, along with its complex poetic style, makes it an outstanding example of the richness and diversity of ancient Indian literature.</div></div></div>
